newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Capital Intelligence reaffirms ICBC ratings.
newsitem.headline: Capital Intelligence reaffirms ICBC ratings.

text.p: Cyprus-based Capital Intelligence reaffirmed ratings of International Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) at A long-term and A-1 short-term, with a stable outlook, it said on Tuesday.
The bank rating agency said its ratings reflected ICBC's "solid asset quality, adequate capital position, strong liquidity, good profitablity and highly regarded management team."

The Federal Reserve of the United States recently imposed penalties on ICBC for alleged inaccurate disclosure of its ownership at the time of its 1984 purchase of its New York-based subsidiary, the Chinese American Bank (CAB).

The principal sanctions were a fine of $5 million, the return of $17.3 million of accumulated priofits from CAB and the requirement to sell its stake in the subsidiary within 300 days, Capital Intelligence said.

The agency said the fine and return of retained income will severely deplete ICBC's 1997 earnings, representing the equivalent of 45 percent of first quarter net profit, though the Bank has sufficient resources to absorb the exceptional cost.
The eventual sale of CAB is likely to generate a net inflow of several times the amount of the penalties, it said.
ICBC is 42.52 percent owned by the Development Fund of the Executive Yuan (the cabinet) and has been listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange since 1979.
Although the government is the bank's largest shareholder, it is run on commercial lines and is largely free from the bureaucracy that hampers the management of banks in the state sector.
But ICBC's close links with the government and its importance in overseas markets mean that support would almost certainly be forthcoming from the authorities in case of need.
